Officer MacLean is disappearing under a pile of paperwork, dreaming of fast car pursuits and major crime busts. Is something finally about to happen?

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram ciùil air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Chaidh Seirm Celtic Connections a chlàradh ann an ionad Platform ann an Glaschu ann a 2022 le feadhainn den luchd-ciùil as fheàrr bho air feadh a RA, Eireann agus às an t-Suain. Anns a’ chiad prògram roghainneach seo gheibhear taghadh de cheòl dùthchasach agus traidiseanta bho Trail West, The Breath, Lena Jonsson Trio agus Brian Finnegan agus a chòmhlan. Seirm Celtic Connections was filmed in Platform, Glasgow in 2022 with appearances from some of the best musicians from the UK, Ireland and Sweden. This first programme features a cross section of music from the world of trad and folk music including Trail West, The Breath, Lena Jonsson Trio and Brian Finnegan and band.

programme.title: Michael Palin and the Mystery of Hammershoi
programme.desc: With a passion for art that is rivalled only by travel, Michael Palin combines both in a European journey to discover more about Vilhelm Hammershoi, an enigmatic Danish artist that has fascinated him for years. Curious to see more of Hammershoi's paintings and discover what kind of life the artist lived, Michael searches for clues in London, Holland and Copenhagen.

programme.title: The Magic of Dance
programme.desc: The first real ballet school was founded by King Louis XIV of France in 1669. From Louis's great palace at Versailles, Margot Fonteyn tells the story of Louis's own love of dancing and how it led from the courtly dances of 17th-century France to the worldwide phenomenon of ballet that we know today. At Drottningholm in Sweden, she visits the Court Theatre and sees ballet performed in the original settings and under the original conditions.

programme.title: Dance Rebels: A Story of Modern Dance
programme.desc: Documentary which tells the compelling story of the mavericks like Isadora Duncan, Martha Graham, Merce Cunningham and Pina Bausch, whose radical ideas created modern dance in the 20th century. With historical archive and the first-hand experiences of student dancers from the Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance, it shows the ideas that challenged audiences and changed dance forever. Also, the biggest stars in dance explain what inspired them to create their own groundbreaking choreography. With contributions from Michael Clark, William Forsythe, Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker, Wayne McGregor, Akram Khan, Boris Charmatz and Lea Anderson.

programme.title: Discovering the World's Table
programme.desc: In Discovering the World's Table, food writer Nick Kwek embarks on a culinary journey in Poland. He visits two of the country's most vibrant cities Warsaw and Poznan to explore how history and culture inspire the food scene. Starting in Warsaw, Nick meets Olga Bradowska, a local food journalist, to learn about the enduring importance of milk bars in Polish cuisine. They are Polish cafeterias that used to provide low-cost, government-subsidised food during the Communist era. Next, Nick travels to the outskirts of the city to Majlert's farm, a family-run business since the 18th century. He joins renowned chef Marcin Przybysz to gather asparagus for his restaurant, which serves dishes based on recipes from prewar cook books. Poznan has a thriving food scene, from Michelin-starred restaurants to trendy cafes. The city offers a mix of traditional Polish cuisine and modern gastronomic trends. Nick uncovers the secrets behind the world's only legally protected croissant, St Martin's croissant, dating back to 1891. He samples the city's famous potatoes and discovers why a smoked beer is considered 'the champagne of Poland'.

programme.title: The Smuggling Business: Undercover
programme.desc: Over the past two years, tens of thousands of migrants have crossed the English Channel in small boats from northern France, despite repeated promises by successive governments to stop the trade. This undercover BBC investigation reveals how people smuggling gangs are operating in plain sight inside a migrant camp in Dunkirk. It exposes a highly organised criminal marketplace driven by fierce competition between rival groups, who enforce control over the settlements through fear, violence and intimidation. The film examines efforts by UK authorities to disrupt and dismantle the criminal networks profiting from the crossings, and questions whether those measures are keeping pace with the scale and sophistication of the operation. BBC investigative reporter Josie Hannett also travels to Crowborough, where opposition to a new asylum seeker accommodation site has turned the town into a flashpoint in the national immigration debate. She asks whether current government policy is likely to deter future arrivals, or whether the UK is preparing for a future that will require many more such sites across the south east

programme.title: The Road to Hope with Fergal Keane
programme.desc: The BBC’s Fergal Keane has spent 40 years witnessing the worst that humanity can do - genocide, war, and famine. So why is he full of hope? The answer lies in the extraordinary bravery he’s encountered in the worst places. In this powerful and humane film by Oscar-winner Alice Doyard, Fergal argues that despite the anxiety of the present we have real cause for hope.

programme.title: Rachel Khoo's Kitchen Notebook
programme.desc: Rachel gets into the swing of a cosmopolitan Riviera town, uncovering foodie gems in Nice's charming back streets. She meets some hip young French chefs cooking with bohemian flair at a small local bistro that prides itself on fresh seasonal produce with a cool laid-back vibe. She also visits a socca bar where she learns about the giant chickpea crépe, a speciality of the region. Back in London, Rachel cooks little socca cakes with ratatouille, confit cod with rainbow chard gratin and mini orange trifles with candied carrots.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The Amazon, where extraordinary animal behaviours reveal the rainforest’s hidden stories. In southern Brazil, over a million turtle hatchlings make a perilous dash to the river as black caiman prey on them – a newly filmed behaviour. In Venezuela, a young harpy eagle that has been watched from its earliest days endures intense storms while awaiting its father’s return with food, providing new understanding of life high in the canopy. Also in Brazil, giant river otters hunt together in a coordinated effort, displaying unique social bonds as they corral fish in the shallows. Army ants in Ecuador break down their bivouac and march through the forest with a level of precision and cooperation seldom seen. In the Pantanal, caiman engage in an elaborate courtship display, their movements sending ripples across the water – a striking look at an ancient ritual.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The frozen north, where survival means constantly adapting to an unforgiving landscape. In Hudson Bay, a rare encounter between the region's top predators unfolds as wolves and polar bears clash over a single carcass – a behaviour never caught on camera until now. Under the glow of the northern lights, snowshoe hares use their large feet to escape lynx in the vast boreal forest. In Alberta, sharp-tailed grouse put on a show like never before, practising their courtship dances under car headlights. Off Alaska’s coast, male walruses engage in curious vocal displays, singing together under the sunset. In summer, millions of salmon begin their epic journey upstream, while newborn caribou navigate dangerous river crossings on their first migratory trek. Life here is a series of bold moves and dramatic encounters, in a place where the stakes are always high.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The Amazon, where extraordinary animal behaviours reveal the rainforest’s hidden stories. In southern Brazil, over a million turtle hatchlings make a perilous dash to the river as black caiman prey on them – a newly filmed behaviour. In Venezuela, a young harpy eagle that has been watched from its earliest days endures intense storms while awaiting its father’s return with food, providing new understanding of life high in the canopy. Also in Brazil, giant river otters hunt together in a coordinated effort, displaying unique social bonds as they corral fish in the shallows. Army ants in Ecuador break down their bivouac and march through the forest with a level of precision and cooperation seldom seen. In the Pantanal, caiman engage in an elaborate courtship display, their movements sending ripples across the water – a striking look at an ancient ritual.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The frozen north, where survival means constantly adapting to an unforgiving landscape. In Hudson Bay, a rare encounter between the region's top predators unfolds as wolves and polar bears clash over a single carcass – a behaviour never caught on camera until now. Under the glow of the northern lights, snowshoe hares use their large feet to escape lynx in the vast boreal forest. In Alberta, sharp-tailed grouse put on a show like never before, practising their courtship dances under car headlights. Off Alaska’s coast, male walruses engage in curious vocal displays, singing together under the sunset. In summer, millions of salmon begin their epic journey upstream, while newborn caribou navigate dangerous river crossings on their first migratory trek. Life here is a series of bold moves and dramatic encounters, in a place where the stakes are always high.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Adam Henson are in Lisburn, Northern Ireland, for the Balmoral Show, the region’s largest agricultural and food event, welcoming more than 100,000 visitors each year. As the show celebrates its 157th year, Sean and Adam meet the people who make it such a vital gathering for the region’s farming community and explore how events like this are crucial to their future. Adam explores heritage crafts that community members are determined to preserve, and he joins families showing their prize livestock. Sean takes charge of the stopwatch at the tractor-handling competition and gets hands-on with traditional local produce that is valuable to the region’s economy.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A pair of artists look to Alistair Appleton to help them find an inspiring rural retreat in Somerset where they can further indulge their creativity. Alistair also meets a young couple who moved to the countryside in search of the good life and never looked back, despite ups and downs along the way.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The Amazon, where extraordinary animal behaviours reveal the rainforest’s hidden stories. In southern Brazil, over a million turtle hatchlings make a perilous dash to the river as black caiman prey on them – a newly filmed behaviour. In Venezuela, a young harpy eagle that has been watched from its earliest days endures intense storms while awaiting its father’s return with food, providing new understanding of life high in the canopy. Also in Brazil, giant river otters hunt together in a coordinated effort, displaying unique social bonds as they corral fish in the shallows. Army ants in Ecuador break down their bivouac and march through the forest with a level of precision and cooperation seldom seen. In the Pantanal, caiman engage in an elaborate courtship display, their movements sending ripples across the water – a striking look at an ancient ritual.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The frozen north, where survival means constantly adapting to an unforgiving landscape. In Hudson Bay, a rare encounter between the region's top predators unfolds as wolves and polar bears clash over a single carcass – a behaviour never caught on camera until now. Under the glow of the northern lights, snowshoe hares use their large feet to escape lynx in the vast boreal forest. In Alberta, sharp-tailed grouse put on a show like never before, practising their courtship dances under car headlights. Off Alaska’s coast, male walruses engage in curious vocal displays, singing together under the sunset. In summer, millions of salmon begin their epic journey upstream, while newborn caribou navigate dangerous river crossings on their first migratory trek. Life here is a series of bold moves and dramatic encounters, in a place where the stakes are always high.

programme.title: Shrek 2
programme.desc: Animated sequel following the grumpy ogre and his bride as they head for the land of Far Far Away to meet her parents. As Shrek contends with his new in-laws, the wicked Fairy Godmother sets in motion a dastardly scheme to scupper his marriage to Fiona. And will any of them survive at the hands of dandy assassin Puss in Boots? Featuring the voices of Mike Myers (Shrek), Eddie Murphy (Donkey), Cameron Diaz (Princess Fiona), Antonio Banderas (Puss in Boots), Julie Andrews (Queen), John Cleese (King), Rupert Everett (Prince Charming), Jennifer Saunders (Fairy Godmother), Aron Warner (Wolf), Kelly Asbury (Page/Elf/Nobleman/Nobleman's Son), Cody Cameron (Pinocchio/Three Pigs) and Conrad Vernon (Gingerbread Man/Cedric/Announcer/Muffin Man).

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Adam Henson are in Lisburn, Northern Ireland, for the Balmoral Show, the region’s largest agricultural and food event, welcoming more than 100,000 visitors each year. As the show celebrates its 157th year, Sean and Adam meet the people who make it such a vital gathering for the region’s farming community and explore how events like this are crucial to their future. Adam explores heritage crafts that community members are determined to preserve, and he joins families showing their prize livestock. Sean takes charge of the stopwatch at the tractor-handling competition and gets hands-on with traditional local produce that is valuable to the region’s economy.

programme.title: Death Valley

programme.desc: In the aftermath of the devastating defeat at Wembley, Southgate’s guilt weighs heavily on his conscience. When the fans then turn on Southgate, accusing him of prioritising politics over performance, he begins to doubt himself ahead of a controversial World Cup in Qatar.

programme.title: UEFA Champions League
programme.desc: Highlights of the 2026 UEFA Champions League final between PSG and Arsenal in Budapest. Twenty years on from their last appearance in the European Cup final, Arsenal are seeking to win their first Champions League title. However, they face a formidable test in the reigning European champions, Paris Saint-Germain. Jason Mohammad presents, with expert analysis from Nedum Onuoha and Matt Upson. Commentary by Steve Wilson and Chris Sutton.

programme.title: Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg
programme.desc: Laura Kuenssberg talks to Nicola Sturgeon, former first minister of Scotland, in her first interview since her husband pleaded guilty to embezzlement. She also interviews Pat McFadden, work and pensions secretary, and Chris Philp, shadow home secretary. And, on the panel, we have former chancellor Jeremy Hunt MP; from Labour, Rosena Allin-Khan MP; and the broadcaster Aasmah Mir.

programme.title: The Book of Life
programme.desc: A museum tour guide explains the Mexican tradition of the Book of Life to a group of bored schoolchildren. They become entranced by the story of Manolo and Joaquin, who vie for the love of the beautiful and feisty Maria.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin wants to run for the hills because of a tricky legal issue in Devon. Jacqui is in Eastbourne, where work is already under way at an end-of-terrace. And Dion goes to Northampton, where a smelly cellar is hard to cope with!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Presenter Eric Knowles is in Peterborough for one of the largest antiques fairs in the UK. He’s joined by Bargain Hunt regular Colin Young, who has some top tips for porcelain collectors. Experts Stephanie Connell and Philip Serrell guide the red and blue teams around the fair, but who will go home empty-handed and who is making a big score?

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The Amazon, where extraordinary animal behaviours reveal the rainforest’s hidden stories. In southern Brazil, over a million turtle hatchlings make a perilous dash to the river as black caiman prey on them – a newly filmed behaviour. In Venezuela, a young harpy eagle that has been watched from its earliest days endures intense storms while awaiting its father’s return with food, providing new understanding of life high in the canopy. Also in Brazil, giant river otters hunt together in a coordinated effort, displaying unique social bonds as they corral fish in the shallows. Army ants in Ecuador break down their bivouac and march through the forest with a level of precision and cooperation seldom seen. In the Pantanal, caiman engage in an elaborate courtship display, their movements sending ripples across the water – a striking look at an ancient ritual.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The frozen north, where survival means constantly adapting to an unforgiving landscape. In Hudson Bay, a rare encounter between the region's top predators unfolds as wolves and polar bears clash over a single carcass – a behaviour never caught on camera until now. Under the glow of the northern lights, snowshoe hares use their large feet to escape lynx in the vast boreal forest. In Alberta, sharp-tailed grouse put on a show like never before, practising their courtship dances under car headlights. Off Alaska’s coast, male walruses engage in curious vocal displays, singing together under the sunset. In summer, millions of salmon begin their epic journey upstream, while newborn caribou navigate dangerous river crossings on their first migratory trek. Life here is a series of bold moves and dramatic encounters, in a place where the stakes are always high.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A pair of artists look to Alistair Appleton to help them find an inspiring rural retreat in Somerset where they can further indulge their creativity. Alistair also meets a young couple who moved to the countryside in search of the good life and never looked back, despite ups and downs along the way.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The Amazon, where extraordinary animal behaviours reveal the rainforest’s hidden stories. In southern Brazil, over a million turtle hatchlings make a perilous dash to the river as black caiman prey on them – a newly filmed behaviour. In Venezuela, a young harpy eagle that has been watched from its earliest days endures intense storms while awaiting its father’s return with food, providing new understanding of life high in the canopy. Also in Brazil, giant river otters hunt together in a coordinated effort, displaying unique social bonds as they corral fish in the shallows. Army ants in Ecuador break down their bivouac and march through the forest with a level of precision and cooperation seldom seen. In the Pantanal, caiman engage in an elaborate courtship display, their movements sending ripples across the water – a striking look at an ancient ritual.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The frozen north, where survival means constantly adapting to an unforgiving landscape. In Hudson Bay, a rare encounter between the region's top predators unfolds as wolves and polar bears clash over a single carcass – a behaviour never caught on camera until now. Under the glow of the northern lights, snowshoe hares use their large feet to escape lynx in the vast boreal forest. In Alberta, sharp-tailed grouse put on a show like never before, practising their courtship dances under car headlights. Off Alaska’s coast, male walruses engage in curious vocal displays, singing together under the sunset. In summer, millions of salmon begin their epic journey upstream, while newborn caribou navigate dangerous river crossings on their first migratory trek. Life here is a series of bold moves and dramatic encounters, in a place where the stakes are always high.

programme.title: Shrek 2
programme.desc: Animated sequel following the grumpy ogre and his bride as they head for the land of Far Far Away to meet her parents. As Shrek contends with his new in-laws, the wicked Fairy Godmother sets in motion a dastardly scheme to scupper his marriage to Fiona. And will any of them survive at the hands of dandy assassin Puss in Boots? Featuring the voices of Mike Myers (Shrek), Eddie Murphy (Donkey), Cameron Diaz (Princess Fiona), Antonio Banderas (Puss in Boots), Julie Andrews (Queen), John Cleese (King), Rupert Everett (Prince Charming), Jennifer Saunders (Fairy Godmother), Aron Warner (Wolf), Kelly Asbury (Page/Elf/Nobleman/Nobleman's Son), Cody Cameron (Pinocchio/Three Pigs) and Conrad Vernon (Gingerbread Man/Cedric/Announcer/Muffin Man).

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Adam Henson are in Lisburn, Northern Ireland, for the Balmoral Show, the region’s largest agricultural and food event, welcoming more than 100,000 visitors each year. As the show celebrates its 157th year, Sean and Adam meet the people who make it such a vital gathering for the region’s farming community and explore how events like this are crucial to their future. Adam explores heritage crafts that community members are determined to preserve, and he joins families showing their prize livestock. Sean takes charge of the stopwatch at the tractor-handling competition and gets hands-on with traditional local produce that is valuable to the region’s economy.

programme.title: 21st Century TV with Lucy Owen
programme.desc: Lucy Owen explores BBC Wales’s news and entertainment archives of 2007. In sport, Tanni Grey-Thompson retires, the Phoenix Cheerleaders come back, and a new digital pet watch monitors children’s exercise. It’s the year we first meet Nessa, find a Led Zeppelin hideaway, and the first air service starts between north and south Wales.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The Amazon, where extraordinary animal behaviours reveal the rainforest’s hidden stories. In southern Brazil, over a million turtle hatchlings make a perilous dash to the river as black caiman prey on them – a newly filmed behaviour. In Venezuela, a young harpy eagle that has been watched from its earliest days endures intense storms while awaiting its father’s return with food, providing new understanding of life high in the canopy. Also in Brazil, giant river otters hunt together in a coordinated effort, displaying unique social bonds as they corral fish in the shallows. Army ants in Ecuador break down their bivouac and march through the forest with a level of precision and cooperation seldom seen. In the Pantanal, caiman engage in an elaborate courtship display, their movements sending ripples across the water – a striking look at an ancient ritual.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The frozen north, where survival means constantly adapting to an unforgiving landscape. In Hudson Bay, a rare encounter between the region's top predators unfolds as wolves and polar bears clash over a single carcass – a behaviour never caught on camera until now. Under the glow of the northern lights, snowshoe hares use their large feet to escape lynx in the vast boreal forest. programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The Amazon, where extraordinary animal behaviours reveal the rainforest’s hidden stories. In southern Brazil, over a million turtle hatchlings make a perilous dash to the river as black caiman prey on them – a newly filmed behaviour. In Venezuela, a young harpy eagle that has been watched from its earliest days endures intense storms while awaiting its father’s return with food, providing new understanding of life high in the canopy. Also in Brazil, giant river otters hunt together in a coordinated effort, displaying unique social bonds as they corral fish in the shallows. Army ants in Ecuador break down their bivouac and march through the forest with a level of precision and cooperation seldom seen. In the Pantanal, caiman engage in an elaborate courtship display, their movements sending ripples across the water – a striking look at an ancient ritual.

programme.title: The Americas
programme.desc: The frozen north, where survival means constantly adapting to an unforgiving landscape. In Hudson Bay, a rare encounter between the region's top predators unfolds as wolves and polar bears clash over a single carcass – a behaviour never caught on camera until now. Under the glow of the northern lights, snowshoe hares use their large feet to escape lynx in the vast boreal forest. In Alberta, sharp-tailed grouse put on a show like never before, practising their courtship dances under car headlights. Off Alaska’s coast, male walruses engage in curious vocal displays, singing together under the sunset. In summer, millions of salmon begin their epic journey upstream, while newborn caribou navigate dangerous river crossings on their first migratory trek. Life here is a series of bold moves and dramatic encounters, in a place where the stakes are always high.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: All the weekend national, UK-wide and international news on Sunday evening at 7.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: When garden space is limited, or just for the joy of growing your own, having an allotment is the perfect pastime. Starting in Calum’s allotment in Leven, we visit the other allotment holders in the Beechgrove team and see them through a whole growing season. At her allotment in Inverleith, Kirsty creates an allotment patch from scratch that is pretty, productive and purple. In Chris’s allotment, high in the Cotswolds, he and wife Frances take on an old disused plot and make it into a low-maintenance vegetable haven. And at his allotment in Joppa, George provides some of his top allotmenteering tips.

programme.title: The Town That Floored the World
programme.desc: How did the Scottish east coast port town of Kirkcaldy become the world centre for linoleum? The Town That Floored the World traces the history of that “magic material” to its origins in the mid 19th century, and tells how one town built its fortunes on its manufacture. Current and former linoleum workers, and Kirkcaldy bairns including crime writer Val McDermid, share their stories of a life in flooring. Lino’s role in high art and design is also traced. Narrated by John Sessions.

programme.title: Wild Cameramen at Work
programme.desc: In the last of this spectacular series on the work of the world's top wildlife film-makers we enter the literally breathtaking environment of the ocean depths. Cameramen Doug Anderson and Doug Allan reveal the technical challenges of filming beneath the waves and encounter animals as diverse as blue whales, white-tip sharks and the unforgettably named weedy sea dragon - a tiny creature whose courtship dance is as tender and graceful as any ballet.

programme.title: The Three Kings
programme.desc: The incredible story of how three men born south of Glasgow, and within 30 miles of each other, grew up to become lifelong friends and three of the most influential men in football history. Matt Busby, Bill Shankly and Jock Stein led Manchester United, Liverpool and Celtic from the doldrums to achieve unimaginable success, captivate millions of fans and become three of the most famous sporting institutions on the planet. With stunning archive footage from their greatest victories and behind-the-scenes access, this story is about more than three men - it is about the makers of modern football.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: While Isa gets into a fix with some cute little animals, Jack and Victor decide to stop putting things off and go on that adventure.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: While helping a blind man do some shopping, Volunteer Officer Ken Beattie discovers there's more to him than meets the eye. Something that also applies to the old pensioner that Officers McLaren and Fletcher rush to rescue. Then these city cops become intoxicated by the drugs they are meant to be guarding. Maggie LeBeau takes us on a tour of her call centre, Desk Sergeant Karen Ann Millar is confronted by a case of cut-price bananas, and countryside cops McIntosh and Mackay arrest a malicious metal detector. Traffic Officers McKirdy and Singh discover that behind the make-up, a criminal clown has a familiar face. Chief Commissioner Miekelson discusses what the Scottish Police Force do with lost property, before he takes part in a local charity golf match. He then does a post-mortem on his appearance before a committee of MSPs.

programme.title: TUNE
programme.desc: Addressing the lack of nightlife for young people in the area, Ullapool native Sigi and his friend Jemima take on the challenge of creating Scotland’s most remote club night. Capturing the action as their electronic music night baile/baile is brought to life, Sigi shares his experience of growing up in this remote part of the county and highlights how important music and community are. From immersion in trad and folk at a young age, to the influence of Martyn Bennett and discovering dance music at Rockness Festival, Sigi shares the journey which brought him home to Ullapool to start a club night for the next generation.

And at his allotment in Joppa, George provides some of his top allotmenteering tips.

programme.title: The Town That Floored the World
programme.desc: How did the Scottish east coast port town of Kirkcaldy become the world centre for linoleum? The Town That Floored the World traces the history of that “magic material” to its origins in the mid 19th century, and tells how one town built its fortunes on its manufacture. Current and former linoleum workers, and Kirkcaldy bairns including crime writer Val McDermid, share their stories of a life in flooring. Lino’s role in high art and design is also traced. Narrated by John Sessions.

programme.title: Wild Cameramen at Work
programme.desc: In the last of this spectacular series on the work of the world's top wildlife film-makers we enter the literally breathtaking environment of the ocean depths. Cameramen Doug Anderson and Doug Allan reveal the technical challenges of filming beneath the waves and encounter animals as diverse as blue whales, white-tip sharks and the unforgettably named weedy sea dragon - a tiny creature whose courtship dance is as tender and graceful as any ballet.

programme.title: The Three Kings
programme.desc: The incredible story of how three men born south of Glasgow, and within 30 miles of each other, grew up to become lifelong friends and three of the most influential men in football history. Matt Busby, Bill Shankly and Jock Stein led Manchester United, Liverpool and Celtic from the doldrums to achieve unimaginable success, captivate millions of fans and become three of the most famous sporting institutions on the planet. With stunning archive footage from their greatest victories and behind-the-scenes access, this story is about more than three men - it is about the makers of modern football.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: While Isa gets into a fix with some cute little animals, Jack and Victor decide to stop putting things off and go on that adventure.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: While helping a blind man do some shopping, Volunteer Officer Ken Beattie discovers there's more to him than meets the eye. Something that also applies to the old pensioner that Officers McLaren and Fletcher rush to rescue. Then these city cops become intoxicated by the drugs they are meant to be guarding. Maggie LeBeau takes us on a tour of her call centre, Desk Sergeant Karen Ann Millar is confronted by a case of cut-price bananas, and countryside cops McIntosh and Mackay arrest a malicious metal detector. Traffic Officers McKirdy and Singh discover that behind the make-up, a criminal clown has a familiar face. Chief Commissioner Miekelson discusses what the Scottish Police Force do with lost property, before he takes part in a local charity golf match. He then does a post-mortem on his appearance before a committee of MSPs.

programme.title: TUNE
programme.desc: Addressing the lack of nightlife for young people in the area, Ullapool native Sigi and his friend Jemima take on the challenge of creating Scotland’s most remote club night. Capturing the action as their electronic music night baile/baile is brought to life, Sigi shares his experience of growing up in this remote part of the county and highlights how important music and community are. From immersion in trad and folk at a young age, to the influence of Martyn Bennett and discovering dance music at Rockness Festival, Sigi shares the journey which brought him home to Ullapool to start a club night for the next generation.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: Now that Gaz and Donna are divorced, Gaz decides the time has come to propose to Janet. Scared that she is losing all her friends, in particular Gaz, Donna insists on helping him organise the proposal, much to the disapproval of Tim who worries she's holding onto the past and not moving on. Gaz and Donna enjoy spending time together, possibly too much, and it conjures up old feelings. Wesley gives Janet a job on the market stall and teaches her the trade, but she struggles as she suffers increasingly from a stomach ache. When the pain gets so bad and she is rushed to hospital, she asks Wesley to phone Gaz, but he is nowhere to be found.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: Janet arrives back from hospital with Wesley and Tim, minus an appendix, and there is no sign of Gaz. Janet catches him out when he comes creeping back into the house later on. When he finds out that she has spent the night with Wesley holding her hand he blurts out that he has slept with Donna, so Janet throws him out. Louise tells Tim she is desperate for a boyfriend, just as ex-boyband member Scott enters the pub. He tries to woo her, but she is convinced there must be something wrong with him. There is, but it's not what she thinks. Gaz is torn between the two girls and although he decides to stay with Janet for the sake of Corinthian, when he goes to tell Donna he realises he loves her too and can't be without her. Janet and Wesley go to the flat only to discover them in bed together once more. They demand he makes a choice between Janet and Donna.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: A social media meltdown forces Geoffrey to reassess his life and values.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: In the near future, the Doctor and Clara find themselves on a space shuttle making a suicide mission to the moon. Crash-landing on the lunar surface, they find a mining base full of corpses, vicious spider-like creatures poised to attack, and a terrible dilemma. When Clara turns to the Doctor for help, she gets the shock of her life.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: The Doctor and Clara are on the most beautiful train in history, speeding among the stars of the future. But a deadly creature is stalking the passengers. Once you see the horrifying mummy, you only have 66 seconds to live. No exceptions, no reprieve. As the Doctor races against the clock, Clara sees him at his deadliest and most ruthless. Will he work out how to defeat the mummy? Start the clock!

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip hits a dead end and rethinks. Digging into Jamie’s recent behaviour and last movements, she realises he may not be an innocent victim after all.

programme.title: Arthur the King
programme.desc: Over the course of ten days and 435 miles, an unbreakable bond is forged between pro adventure racer Michael Light and a scrappy street dog companion dubbed Arthur. Desperate for one last chance to win, Michael convinces a sponsor to back him and a team of athletes for the Adventure Racing World Championship in the Dominican Republic. As the team is pushed to their outer limits of endurance in the race, Arthur redefines what victory, loyalty and friendship truly mean. Based on a true story.

programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: With the England team at an all-time low after an embarrassing defeat to Iceland, Gareth Southgate becomes the new manager. Haunted by his own penalty miss with England, he inherits a broken team and a jaded fanbase. With psychologist Pippa Grange, he sets about changing the team’s mindset and tackling his and England’s biggest fear – penalties.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Sammi Kinghorn explore the forests of the Welsh valleys at a critical time. As spring gives way to summer, wildlife is at its most active and visitor numbers rise, but wildfires pose a growing threat. They meet the people shaping the future of these landscapes, from fire prevention and recreation to conservation and training the next generation. Meanwhile, Tom Heap heads to Devon and Cornwall to investigate the state of the UK’s seaweed farming industry.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Some more unusual methods of growing are demonstrated at Beechgrove Garden. Ruth Vichos attempts to produce a mushroom crop and there’s a report on some of Scotland’s best bonsai, with everything you need to know to start that form of cultivation. Brian Cunningham is in the Seaside Garden at Beechgrove refreshing the planting with varieties that can withstand a coastal climate and Brian turns conifers into sculptures with topiary. Plus the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie visits Bee Edge Farm near Eyemouth to help open the barn doors and let the cows out for summer. Continuing to mark Landward’s 50th anniversary, Cammy catches up with a farming pioneer who was never one for sitting on the fence, and Rosie is stepping back in time in Aberdeenshire to find out what one old farm building can tell us about our agricultural past. Elsewhere, Leanna is on the trail of a walrus that has been turning up in harbours around Scotland's north coast.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Imad Alarnab brings a taste of Syria to the studio with his Middle Eastern feast – mujadara, pickled cucumbers, laban bikhiar and baba ganoush. Shivi Ramoutar has the perfect recipe for a fried fish taco, finished with a punchy green mango chow and tamarind pepper sauce. Patrick Williams serves the flavours of South Africa with his peri-peri poussin with confit potatoes, while Jacob Kenedy prepares two simple but tasty granitas. Pastry perfectionist Ravneet Gill rustles up a delightful summertime strawberry and custard tart, and Laura Smyth faces either her food heaven or her food hell. Meanwhile, Rick Stein takes to the shores of Cornwall to forage for razor clams, and the Hairy Bikers head to Tewkesbury to learn all about mustard balls.

programme.title: Athletics: Great Manchester Run
programme.desc: Live coverage of the 2026 Great Manchester Run.

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Suppers
programme.desc: Nigel Slater creates simple but delicious meals from ingredients that are often overlooked, including a lentil and chard stew.

programme.title: Mary Berry - Cook and Share
programme.desc: Dame Mary Berry goes behind the scenes at a huge wedding, sharing memories of her own special day and cooking up some delicious dishes perfect for sharing at special occasions.

programme.title: Operation Crossbow
programme.desc: World War II drama. A small group of agents is sent on a vital mission to destroy a Nazi V-2 rocket base in Holland. Their aim is to prevent flying bombs from falling on London.

programme.title: The Searchers
programme.desc: Classic John Ford western. Believing the Comanche have abducted his young niece, embittered Ethan Edwards sets out to save her, accompanied by hot-headed Martin. But their long quest takes its toll.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve and the team head to the Tian Shan mountains of Kyrgyzstan to find one of the world’s most endangered big cats – the snow leopard. Kyrgyzstan sits at the heart of the global snow leopard population, but from the Himalayas in the south to Russia in the north, snow leopards are under threat right across their range. The goal of this expedition is to explore the remote and impenetrable Djangart valley. Snow leopards are known to live north and south of here, but nothing is known about what lies between. No one has studied the cats here because these high-altitude peaks are so difficult to access, but this region is packed with precious minerals, and mining companies now have their sights firmly set on the Djangart valley. Teaming up with Kyrgyz conservation group Snow Leopard Foundation, Steve and the team set out to find evidence of a breeding population of snow leopards. If they can find snow leopards living and breeding here, they hope to persuade the government of Kyrgyzstan to turn the Djangart valley into a protected nature reserve.

programme.title: Southbank at 75: You Are Here
programme.desc: An epic dance spectacular and electrifying journey through 75 years of British youth culture to mark Southbank Centre’s landmark birthday. This is a freewheeling journey of discovery across decades, remixing and reimagining some of the most vivid and influential youth and social movements that have driven culture forward since 1951, when the south bank of the Thames hosted the Festival of Britain.

programme.title: Athletics: Diamond League
programme.desc: Coverage from the 2026 Diamond League meeting at Rabat, Morocco.

programme.title: The Mother of All Cons
programme.desc: In 2010, poorly 16-year-old Megan Bhari decides to launch a charity for seriously ill children. She’s battling a brain tumour, and knowing the toll illness can take, she decides to devote her life to creating fairy-tale experiences that might help children to forget, even briefly, that they’re sick. Believe in Magic becomes an immediate success. Inspired by Megan’s courage and self-sacrifice, celebrities and her beloved One Direction are more than willing to donate their time and money to the cause. And when her mother, Jean, posts news that Megan’s health has deteriorated and she needs expensive treatment in America, countless families and celebrity supporters rally around to support Meg. Together, they raise the money needed overnight. However, in an online chat, some parents whose own children have been treated for cancer abroad begin asking questions.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools welcomes vocal powerhouse Jessie Ware, pop star Holly Humberstone, prolific producer Jack Antonoff, soul singer Samm Henshaw, electro duo Fcukers and director Tim Pope.

programme.title: The Blues Brothers
programme.desc: Jake Blues rejoins his brother Elwood after being released from prison, but the duo have just days to reunite their old R&B band and save the Catholic home where the two were raised, outrunning the police as they tear through Chicago.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce presents a special episode devoted to one of the most significant and consequential issues of our age: artificial intelligence. On the panel are: from the government, Darren Jones, chief secretary to the prime minister; Julia Lopez, shadow secretary of state for science, innovation and technology; Mo Gawdat, author, entrepreneur and former chief business officer at Google X; Laura Gilbert, senior director of AI at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change; and Victor Riparbelli, founder and CEO of London-based AI company Synthesia.

Shivi Ramoutar has the perfect recipe for a fried fish taco, finished with a punchy green mango chow and tamarind pepper sauce. Patrick Williams serves the flavours of South Africa with his peri-peri poussin with confit potatoes, while Jacob Kenedy prepares two simple but tasty granitas. Pastry perfectionist Ravneet Gill rustles up a delightful summertime strawberry and custard tart, and Laura Smyth faces either her food heaven or her food hell. Meanwhile, Rick Stein takes to the shores of Cornwall to forage for razor clams, and the Hairy Bikers head to Tewkesbury to learn all about mustard balls.

programme.title: Operation Crossbow
programme.desc: World War II drama. A small group of agents is sent on a vital mission to destroy a Nazi V-2 rocket base in Holland. Their aim is to prevent flying bombs from falling on London.

programme.title: The Searchers
programme.desc: Classic John Ford western. Believing the Comanche have abducted his young niece, embittered Ethan Edwards sets out to save her, accompanied by hot-headed Martin. But their long quest takes its toll.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve and the team head to the Tian Shan mountains of Kyrgyzstan to find one of the world’s most endangered big cats – the snow leopard. Kyrgyzstan sits at the heart of the global snow leopard population, but from the Himalayas in the south to Russia in the north, snow leopards are under threat right across their range. The goal of this expedition is to explore the remote and impenetrable Djangart valley. Snow leopards are known to live north and south of here, but nothing is known about what lies between. No one has studied the cats here because these high-altitude peaks are so difficult to access, but this region is packed with precious minerals, and mining companies now have their sights firmly set on the Djangart valley. Teaming up with Kyrgyz conservation group Snow Leopard Foundation, Steve and the team set out to find evidence of a breeding population of snow leopards. If they can find snow leopards living and breeding here, they hope to persuade the government of Kyrgyzstan to turn the Djangart valley into a protected nature reserve.

programme.title: Southbank at 75: You Are Here

programme.title: The Mother of All Cons
programme.desc: In 2010, poorly 16-year-old Megan Bhari decides to launch a charity for seriously ill children. She’s battling a brain tumour, and knowing the toll illness can take, she decides to devote her life to creating fairy-tale experiences that might help children to forget, even briefly, that they’re sick. Believe in Magic becomes an immediate success. Inspired by Megan’s courage and self-sacrifice, celebrities and her beloved One Direction are more than willing to donate their time and money to the cause. And when her mother, Jean, posts news that Megan’s health has deteriorated and she needs expensive treatment in America, countless families and celebrity supporters rally around to support Meg. Together, they raise the money needed overnight. However, in an online chat, some parents whose own children have been treated for cancer abroad begin asking questions.

programme.title: Chuggington
programme.desc: Being a super chugger is hard work! But when given a well deserved day off, Action Chugger has a hard time relaxing. Can the trainees get Action Chugger to finally rest his wheels?

programme.desc: Supertato and Tomato find themselves stuck in a slippery bathtub, whilst Evil Pea rampages around the supermarket on a giant soap-squirting machine.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing is waiting to sit in the fire engine at the park. Pando and Sula both get a turn, but when it is Bing's go there is an emergency and the fire engine has to leave! Flop, Amma, Sula and Bing walk to Bing's house for carroty bagels and Bing's 'Fabulous Fire Engine Facts' book. But outside the neighbour's house is the fire engine! Arlo is stuck on the roof, and Bing has to help him get down.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are playing outside, when out of a bush jumps the cutest creature they ever did see. They think it is simply adorable and tell it so… with startling results. The creature bursts into tears! The creature, whose name is Plinky, tells them her whole family are monsters, and that’s what she’s supposed to be, but she just cannot get the hang of it. The Squirrels are keen to help Plinky get in touch with her scary side. Fortunately, Duggee has his monster badge.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The day starts when Duggee moves a cupboard, and the Squirrels find a dusty, old book behind it. It’s Duggee’s diary from when he was a teenager! The Squirrels aren’t sure what a diary is, so Duggee explains by reading some extracts. The Squirrels are keen to write diaries of their own.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: When Glitch crash lands at the Go Jet Academy, he’s furious to see that his accident was caused by a flowery plant blocking Grim HQ’s chimneys. But Tala loves this plant and plans to grow some of the rare flowers in her research garden. Glitch decides to do the same, setting the Grimbots to create the perfect conditions for the plants to grow. But Tala and Foz soon find out that the plant is actually a superweed which grows so fast that it threatens to overwhelm the island! Can the Go Jetters stop the weed from damaging the Academy and Grim HQ?

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: After Shellington crashes the Gup-D, he and Kwazii team up with a moray eel and grouper fish to pick up the pieces.

programme.desc: Fergie is sad and disappointed when a sudden apple allergy means that she can’t eat her favourite food or do her favourite activity - apple picking! But luckily, her favourite friends will stop at nothing to brighten her spirits. Together, they set up a Fergie Tree full of all her other favourite things!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo teach Unicorse good manners, so he can ask Mum out on a date.

programme.desc: The Squirrels notice that Happy looks and seems different – he is frowning, his smile is upside down, and he’s wearing new trainers! When they check in on him, Happy is frustrated, but he can’t seem to identify where his frustration is coming from. They turn to Duggee for help, who uses his feeling cards to explain an array of feelings to Happy. All the Squirrels help by relaying their past experiences and the feelings that they evoked.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After overhearing Duggee listening to a beautiful track by the Squirrel Valley Voices Choir, the Squirrels seek to learn more about the roles that make up a choir – basses, sopranos, altos and tenors. A distressed Eugene then alerts them that half of the choir have been taken sick and can’t perform that day. The Squirrels step up to take their place. Initially, when the newly arranged choir sing, the voices aren’t gelling together. Duggee teaches them the principles they must get right first, for the choir to succeed – breathing, pitch, volume, focus and timing. With a lot of practice, the Squirrels turn up to perform perfectly together and finally earn their Choir Badge.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Gadabout gives himself dance fever to prove he is as much fun as Zog and Pearl. When he can't stop boogieing, they must cure him before sunset so he is not stuck dancing forever!

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piripenguins face a few tricky problems, but they discover that swapping items and working together can provide clever solutions, turning a regular day into an extraordinary one.

programme.desc: Rafi promises her dads she will go straight to bed while Aunty T babysits. But when Aunty T suggests night-time ice cream, Rafi makes a wish and her bed magically flies them out into Manchester! It’s exciting at first, but soon Rafi becomes sleepy and wants to go home. Suddenly, the wish runs out and the bed drops onto a tree. Luckily, Aunty T uses her umbrella to magic them safely back. Rafi realises bedtime is bedtime for a reason.

programme.desc: A stuck baby Kiwimammathus needs help from Ginger and baby Pea-Rexes to get back home.

programme.title: Spidey and His Amazing Friends

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond

programme.title: Stan Can

They see all the wonders of the underwater world, including a giant sea stallion and some jazz fish. And to the Squirrels, all those coloured buttons that work the submarine are just as interesting as what is outside. Betty's dad has a tricky time amusing the Squirrels. Thank goodness for the school of fish!

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Sunny gets a tummy ache from not washing his hands, so Vida teaches him all about germs - and helps his tummy!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Glitch's giant drill causes a dino disaster for the team's fossil hunt in the Gobi Desert.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants to swim with both her dads, but Jake feels nervous in the pool. Rafi makes a wish, and suddenly they all have mermaid tails! Jake isn’t sure at first, but with Rafi’s help, he learns to flip his tail and swim. When the wish ends, Jake is back on his feet and feels braver than before. Rafi understands that everyone gains courage in their own time, and the family share a happy hug.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Stripes worries that the Sundial Stage isn’t loud enough when his guitar hero comes to play a gig. With Yukee’s help, Stripes is determined to turn the volume up to 11... but is that too loud?

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button use kitchen foil to create and launch an out-of-this-world spaceship.

programme.title: Something Special

programme.title: The Toddler Club
programme.desc: Nigel, Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear welcome toddlers Seren, Ella, Dylan, Erin and Boe, and their grown-ups, to the Toddler Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! The What’s in the Box? game reveals a toy telephone, and when the toddlers and parents open up a bigger box, they discover lots more objects and toys that are inspired by a 'let's chat' theme. This subject is explored through play, song and story. Grown-ups are encouraged to take part at home by hiding a safe, toddler-appropriate 'let's chat' toy or object inside a recycled box for them to reveal and explore with their toddler! Storytime is all about joining in with the words, as Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear play a game of Follow the Leader! Viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring the 'let's chat' theme too. And, The Benjee and Bailee Say Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with stretching and the Goodbye song.

programme.title: Vegesaurs

programme.title: Nanny Mcphee
programme.desc: Fantasy family comedy. Recently-widowed Cedric Brown struggles to control his brood of seven children, who have managed to drive away 17 different nannies with their bad behaviour - when Cedric arranges for the mysterious Nanny McPhee to come and look after the children, led by the precocious Simon, the children attempt to scare her in the same way as they have the others, but it soon becomes clear that their bad behaviour brings about supernatural and eerie reprisals... Meanwhile, Cedric's uptight Aunt Adelaide has insisted that unless he finds a new wife within a month, she will take one of the children into custody. With their father's utter hopelessness at courtship common knowledge and facing a future in the workhouse - or worse, in the care of relatives, the children turn to their new nanny to save the day.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. The pressure intensifies as the final looms. A quiz produces unexpected results, leaving one player desperate to be believed for once, while Billy continues with a high-risk bluff designed to frame Harry and control the narrative. Valuation descends into chaos. Accusations fly, emotions boil over and the vote collapses into deadlock. When a rule is broken, the hosts are forced to intervene, triggering a dramatic reversal and a shock exit that reshapes the game. A final quiz redraws the leaderboard before a brutal twist is introduced: players are offered the chance to leave immediately with their winnings. As night falls, the house faces an impossible choice — risk everything, or walk away.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: The Assembly returns with never-before-seen questions and moments from across its second series. Stephen Fry reveals more about his wild past, Nicola Sturgeon bonds over Cilla Black and long johns, Rylan opens up about grief, and Anna Maxwell Martin takes on a chaotic game of question tennis. Across the episode, there are outrageous questions, poignant reflections, moments of pure joy and toilet breaks. Lenny Henry looks back on racial divides, comedy and his early career, Aitch talks family, fame and friendship, and Nicola Sturgeon reflects movingly on being child-free and the life she built outside politics. From cocaine smuggling and Supermarket Sweep secrets to EastEnders impressions, this is The Assembly - unseen and unmissable.

programme.title: Cape Rock Killer

As 12 jurors are sworn in for the trial, they find that their own lives are changed by the experience.

programme.title: Cape Rock Killer
programme.desc: Legal drama series exploring the lives and loves of 12 ordinary citizens at a murder trial. In court, Amanda's ex gives heartfelt testimony, but Colby pokes holes in his story. programme.title: Nanny Mcphee
programme.desc: Fantasy family comedy. Recently-widowed Cedric Brown struggles to control his brood of seven children, who have managed to drive away 17 different nannies with their bad behaviour - when Cedric arranges for the mysterious Nanny McPhee to come and look after the children, led by the precocious Simon, the children attempt to scare her in the same way as they have the others, but it soon becomes clear that their bad behaviour brings about supernatural and eerie reprisals... Meanwhile, Cedric's uptight Aunt Adelaide has insisted that unless he finds a new wife within a month, she will take one of the children into custody. With their father's utter hopelessness at courtship common knowledge and facing a future in the workhouse - or worse, in the care of relatives, the children turn to their new nanny to save the day.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. The pressure intensifies as the final looms. A quiz produces unexpected results, leaving one player desperate to be believed for once, while Billy continues with a high-risk bluff designed to frame Harry and control the narrative. Valuation descends into chaos. Accusations fly, emotions boil over and the vote collapses into deadlock. When a rule is broken, the hosts are forced to intervene, triggering a dramatic reversal and a shock exit that reshapes the game. A final quiz redraws the leaderboard before a brutal twist is introduced: players are offered the chance to leave immediately with their winnings. As night falls, the house faces an impossible choice — risk everything, or walk away.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: The Assembly returns with never-before-seen questions and moments from across its second series. Stephen Fry reveals more about his wild past, Nicola Sturgeon bonds over Cilla Black and long johns, Rylan opens up about grief, and Anna Maxwell Martin takes on a chaotic game of question tennis. Across the episode, there are outrageous questions, poignant reflections, moments of pure joy and toilet breaks. Lenny Henry looks back on racial divides, comedy and his early career, Aitch talks family, fame and friendship, and Nicola Sturgeon reflects movingly on being child-free and the life she built outside politics. From cocaine smuggling and Supermarket Sweep secrets to EastEnders impressions, this is The Assembly - unseen and unmissable.

programme.title: Cape Rock Killer
programme.desc: Legal drama series exploring the lives and loves of 12 ordinary citizens at a murder trial. programme.title: Cape Rock Killer
programme.desc: Legal drama series exploring the lives and loves of 12 ordinary citizens at a murder trial. In court, Amanda's ex gives heartfelt testimony, but Colby pokes holes in his story. programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Joining Alan Titchmarsh at Manor Farm are Stephen Tompkinson and West End and Broadway star Kerry Ellis. We go behind the scenes at the Globe Theatre ahead of their summer season, and Queen of Herbs Jekka McVicar says 'I do' with herbs with a romantic tale in time for wedding season. Plus, wine expert Toni Osoba has the very best in summer sparkles, and we hear from one woman who gave up her job as a nurse to become a farmer - and she joins us with three of her impressive Highland cows.

programme.title: Nanny Mcphee
programme.desc: Fantasy family comedy. Recently-widowed Cedric Brown struggles to control his brood of seven children, who have managed to drive away 17 different nannies with their bad behaviour - when Cedric arranges for the mysterious Nanny McPhee to come and look after the children, led by the precocious Simon, the children attempt to scare her in the same way as they have the others, but it soon becomes clear that their bad behaviour brings about supernatural and eerie reprisals... Meanwhile, Cedric's uptight Aunt Adelaide has insisted that unless he finds a new wife within a month, she will take one of the children into custody. With their father's utter hopelessness at courtship common knowledge and facing a future in the workhouse - or worse, in the care of relatives, the children turn to their new nanny to save the day.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. The pressure intensifies as the final looms. A quiz produces unexpected results, leaving one player desperate to be believed for once, while Billy continues with a high-risk bluff designed to frame Harry and control the narrative. Valuation descends into chaos. Accusations fly, emotions boil over and the vote collapses into deadlock. When a rule is broken, the hosts are forced to intervene, triggering a dramatic reversal and a shock exit that reshapes the game. A final quiz redraws the leaderboard before a brutal twist is introduced: players are offered the chance to leave immediately with their winnings. As night falls, the house faces an impossible choice — risk everything, or walk away.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: The Assembly returns with never-before-seen questions and moments from across its second series. Stephen Fry reveals more about his wild past, Nicola Sturgeon bonds over Cilla Black and long johns, Rylan opens up about grief, and Anna Maxwell Martin takes on a chaotic game of question tennis. Across the episode, there are outrageous questions, poignant reflections, moments of pure joy and toilet breaks. Lenny Henry looks back on racial divides, comedy and his early career, Aitch talks family, fame and friendship, and Nicola Sturgeon reflects movingly on being child-free and the life she built outside politics. From cocaine smuggling and Supermarket Sweep secrets to EastEnders impressions, this is The Assembly - unseen and unmissable.

programme.title: Cape Rock Killer
programme.desc: Legal drama series exploring the lives and loves of 12 ordinary citizens at a murder trial. As 12 jurors are sworn in for the trial, they find that their own lives are changed by the experience.

programme.title: Cape Rock Killer
programme.desc: Legal drama series exploring the lives and loves of 12 ordinary citizens at a murder trial. In court, Amanda's ex gives heartfelt testimony, but Colby pokes holes in his story. Pressure rises as Beth, wife of the accused, takes the stand and Nicholls lands a blow that shakes her. Outside court, Bassam's stepdaughter learns of his sacking and is upset he won't fight it. Gretel tries to unravel her night with Jazmyn but finds only troubling blanks.

programme.title: Nanny Mcphee
programme.desc: Fantasy family comedy. Recently-widowed Cedric Brown struggles to control his brood of seven children, who have managed to drive away 17 different nannies with their bad behaviour - when Cedric arranges for the mysterious Nanny McPhee to come and look after the children, led by the precocious Simon, the children attempt to scare her in the same way as they have the others, but it soon becomes clear that their bad behaviour brings about supernatural and eerie reprisals... Meanwhile, Cedric's uptight Aunt Adelaide has insisted that unless he finds a new wife within a month, she will take one of the children into custody. With their father's utter hopelessness at courtship common knowledge and facing a future in the workhouse - or worse, in the care of relatives, the children turn to their new nanny to save the day.

As night falls, the house faces an impossible choice — risk everything, or walk away.

programme.title: The Assembly

From cocaine smuggling and Supermarket Sweep secrets to EastEnders impressions, this is The Assembly - unseen and unmissable.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. The pressure intensifies as the final looms. A quiz produces unexpected results, leaving one player desperate to be believed for once, while Billy continues with a high-risk bluff designed to frame Harry and control the narrative. Valuation descends into chaos. Accusations fly, emotions boil over and the vote collapses into deadlock. When a rule is broken, the hosts are forced to intervene, triggering a dramatic reversal and a shock exit that reshapes the game. A final quiz redraws the leaderboard before a brutal twist is introduced: players are offered the chance to leave immediately with their winnings. As night falls, the house faces an impossible choice — risk everything, or walk away.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: The Assembly returns with never-before-seen questions and moments from across its second series. Stephen Fry reveals more about his wild past, Nicola Sturgeon bonds over Cilla Black and long johns, Rylan opens up about grief, and Anna Maxwell Martin takes on a chaotic game of question tennis. Across the episode, there are outrageous questions, poignant reflections, moments of pure joy and toilet breaks. Lenny Henry looks back on racial divides, comedy and his early career, Aitch talks family, fame and friendship, and Nicola Sturgeon reflects movingly on being child-free and the life she built outside politics. From cocaine smuggling and Supermarket Sweep secrets to EastEnders impressions, this is The Assembly - unseen and unmissable.

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: Comedy-drama series providing an honest, uplifting and heart-warming portrayal of teenagers from Liverpool. When Ted is paired with 14-year-old Albie in a school mentoring programme, the deeper issue of Albie's struggles with anorexia become apparent to Ted - he tries to offer help to Albie by revealing his own self-esteem issues, but Albie continually denies that he has problems and mocks Ted for his 'saviour complex'. When Ted gets a chance to showcase his comedic talent on stage, Albie has a breakdown due to his anorexia and calls Ted for help - Ted ignores him as he is sick of how Albie treats him, but when he finds out that Albie is in hospital, he visits and offers heartfelt support that is finally welcomed by Albie. Elsewhere, Aimee and Christopher are dating after getting together over the summer, Reece connects with his dad Alan during a karaoke night, Jodie attempts to restart her career but struggles with confidence, and Mia-Louise meets a new online video gaming partner.

programme.title: Rosemary & Thyme
programme.desc: Light-hearted drama series about a pair of sleuthing gardeners. Rosemary's maternal side is brought out when she and Laura find an abandoned baby under a gooseberry bush in Penelope Braxton's garden - Penelope is remarrying her ex-husband Tim and our heroines are working on a memorial garden as an intended wedding present from Penelope to Tim. Rosemary and Laura are forced to care for the baby as they try to find out who the mother is and why she would abandon him, but events take a dramatic turn when neighbouring artist Sir Carlos Potter is found murdered - how is he connected, will the girls be able to reunite mother and baby, and will Rosemary remain enchanted by the prospect of bringing up a child?

programme.title: Rosemary & Thyme
programme.desc: Light-hearted drama series about a pair of sleuthing gardeners. Laura's son Matthew and his friends are on an annual tennis holiday at a beautiful tennis camp in southern Spain that is owned by former champion Ray Parfitt - meanwhile, Laura and Rosemary are creating a trophy garden for a pro-am tennis tournament that Ray is holding. When one of the players is found dead after a night out, everyone assumes that it was a drunken accident but the girls suspect foul play - as Rosemary rediscovers the thrill of riding motor scooters in the neighbouring village of Mija while Laura finds the local bullring to be a mysterious and threatening place, the value of property proves to be the driving force for evil in this idyllic sun-drenched resort.

programme.title: Rosemary & Thyme
programme.desc: Light-hearted drama series. Rosemary's cousin Charles is performing with an amateur dramatic group and Rosemary and Laura have been brought along to prepare the garden of the Open Air Theatre in time for opening night - everyone is deeply shocked when one of the actors accidentally shoots himself during rehearsal, but the police then discover the gun was loaded with live ammunition and not blanks. It becomes apparent that there is a murderer in their midst - was the bullet intended for Adam, or the theatre's philanthropist Victor Channing? As Victor's wife Jenny gets stage fright, her role in the play is given to Laura to Rosemary's displeasure - with opening night fast approaching, Rosemary struggles to complete the garden on her own as Laura, who is delighted with her part, becomes more involved with the production. Will the play go without a hitch, or is someone out to sabotage it?

programme.title: Agatha Christie's Marple
programme.desc: Crime thriller featuring the author's much-loved spinster sleuth. Miss Marple investigates when her holiday at an old school friend's coastal villa is interrupted by the mysterious death of one of her fellow guests just hours after he told the ghostly tale of a murderous child.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Crime drama series. Careful not to be seen, Samantha Berry slips away from Whitcombe Grange - while dressed in Georgian period attire - on her way to a secret rendezvous. Unaware that a drone is filming her, she is then stabbed to death by an unseen assailant... With Kam away on a course, Barnaby and Winter meet locum pathologist Petra Antonescu and she informs them that the victim was stabbed with a feather quill pen - however, Barnaby is puzzled to find a syringe lying nearby. Tracing Samantha to the Grange, Barnaby and Winter meet owners James and Kitty Oswood - who explain that they host Jane Austen experience weekends - and Winter learns from the Oswoods' rebellious daughter Polly that Samantha kept asking questions about the house and village. When Samantha is found to be a journalist with a special interest in the local village's new delivery service for prescriptions by drone, Barnaby and Winter need to look back in time if they are to find her killer.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Crime drama series. The annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival draws in big audiences as several musicians anxiously compete for the coveted Falconer Bursary Award - shockwaves rocket though it when Jacob Wheeler is awarded the prize instead of the supremely talented Zac Sowande, but shock soon turns to horror when Jacob is found murdered strangled by violin string. Barnaby's initial investigations begin by focusing on Jacob's fellow musicians and their charismatic maestro Michael Falconer, who is using the festival to debut his Ninth Symphony while simultaneously belittling his own musician son Dan - when Barnaby realises that Jacob's Stradivarius is missing and that Jacob might not have been the completely dedicated musician his sister Natalie claims him to be, his subsequent investigations lead them deep into a world that is haunted by a potentially deadly curse.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Causton is buzzing at the opening of a new brewery on the site of a famously cursed Abbey. However, excitement turns to fear when a man is found boiled to death in one of the vats. DCI Barnaby and DS Winter are puzzled; could this really be about beer?

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: When Mahesh Sidana - a butterfly collector and founding member of an elite IQ society - is found murdered after being pinned to a wall in a manner similar to his treasured butterfly specimens, DCI Barnaby and DS Winter are thrust into a crime that impacts not only on their community, but internationally. Can they catch the culprit - with the help of an old friend - before another victim is found?

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: Detective drama series based on the novels by Ann Cleeves. After two young people are killed in the same way - drowned and surrounded by flowers - DCI Vera Stanhope knows that she must catch the murderer before they strike again. As the friends' loyalty turns to betrayal, Vera finds that a small act of teenage blackmail and an illicit affair may have driven someone to kill.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: There is a space invasion under Jon Arbuckle's roof, and the aliens are looking very much like Garfield's favourite meal: lasagnas.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Squeak and his mice family have taken up residence in Garfield's house, to Jon's despair, who will deprive Garfield of lasagnas if he doesn't turn things back to normal.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield's favourite restaurant, Vito's Pizzeria, is in jeopardy. The evil Mama Meany wants to buy it to expand his own restaurant, with the PizzaGrand 7000 capable of making ten pizzas a minute.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: A mother bluebird is locked in a neighbourhood garage, so who will care for her eggs? That's a job for Garfield, who is sometimes quite a mother hen.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Odie is found by Al the Dogcatcher with no license on his collar so he puts him in the city pound with other stray dogs. Garfield will do everything to get his friend back.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Odie falls in love with a brush. Garfield becomes a little bit jealous about that and decides to make the brush disappear.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Jon finds an old accordion. It's unbearable for Garfield who totally dislikes this music. He will do everything to get rid of it.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Jon has won a live turkey in a raffle and wants to prepare it for dinner, but he can't make up his mind to eat it. Neither can Garfield!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield and Odie are watching a horror movie... They're scared. Jon, who has forgotten his key, is knocking at the door. The two pets won't let him in until he's proven his identity.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield is angry. A fake, secret agent is trying to steal the show and his popularity among his friends.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: It's Halloween! Garfield goes trick or treating and disguises himself as a scary Catzilla. But the real Catzilla has just escaped from the city zoo and will spread panic in Garfield's neighbourhood.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Odie has been thrown out of the house by Garfield and spends all night outside on his own. An alien crashes his UFO in the garden and loses a key part necessary to get back home!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Nermal's owner has gone away on vacation and Jon has offered to look after Nermal while he's gone. Watch out, everybody! The cutest kitten in the world (he says so himself) is coming over for a week!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Who has stolen Pooky? After a night drying on the clothes line, Pooky has disappeared, and Garfield can't sleep without him.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
